findings.text: s28 blames a station-sourced answer that "has gone stale during a long derivation" while the station's health beat stayed fresh, but both readers take their age from the same single `heartbeat` row of the station table: `_read_station_document` returns the document with `_station_markers(connection)` read in the same cursor (obligation_snapshot.py:556-578), `read_station_answer` derives `stale` from that beat (obligation_snapshot.py:688-689), `read_station_tick` reads the same markers and the same age (obligation_snapshot.py:605-619), and the beat thread writes that row every 5 s off its own handle independent of the tick (`STATION_BEAT_SECONDS = 5.0`, `StationBeat.beat_once`, station.py:90,141-148) with the guard refusing only after lease loss (station_store.py:209-215). A probe of the real readers over one store returned answer stale/beat_age and tick stale/beat_age identical in all four states (fresh beat 0/0; beat stopped 600 s 600/600; beat stopped with a running tick recorded 600/600; fresh beat with that running tick 0/0). So on the station's own node the fresh-beat case never reaches the tick consult at all (`tick = station` unless the source is the snapshot, watch_unit.py:1084-1091): the "fresh tick is never asked" sentence needs a state the store cannot produce

That measures the branch, not the system the section describes as its reference
